---
title: "Set up Python"
subtitle: "About 15 minutes. Do it before the session if you can; we'll also do it together at the start."
---

::: {.callout-note}
## Stuck? Colab is the backup

We do the install together at the start of the session. Around 9:30, if your notebook still won't run, switch to
Google Colab ([step 10](#colab)) and keep going. A helper will finish your install at the break or during practice
time.
:::

## 1. Open a terminal

A terminal is a window where you type commands instead of clicking.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Mac

Press {{< kbd Cmd-Space >}}, type **Terminal**, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}.

### Windows

Press the {{< kbd Win >}} key, type **PowerShell**, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}. Your prompt starts with `PS C:\`.
:::

## 2. Install uv

uv is one small tool that installs Python and the packages you need. It needs no admin rights. Copy the line for your
computer, paste it into the terminal, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Mac

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```
:::

### Windows (PowerShell)

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```
:::
:::

## 3. Check it worked

**Close the terminal and open a new one**, so it can find uv. Then run:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv --version
```
:::

You should see a version number, like `uv {{< var checked.uv >}}`.

## 4. Make your project folder

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv init --python {{< var python >}} --vcs none dss-python
cd dss-python
```
:::

The folder is made in your home folder: `/Users/<you>/dss-python` on a Mac, `C:\Users\<you>\dss-python` on Windows.
uv puts three starter files in it, `pyproject.toml`, `main.py` and `README.md`. Leave them alone.

- `--python {{< var python >}}` matches the Python that Colab uses, so code behaves the same in both places.
- `--vcs none` skips git, so a Mac without Apple's developer tools doesn't ask to install them.

## 5. Add JupyterLab and matplotlib

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv add jupyterlab matplotlib
```
:::

uv downloads Python {{< var python >}}, JupyterLab and matplotlib into one environment, a hidden `.venv` folder inside
`dss-python`. JupyterLab, its Python and matplotlib all live there, so the bar plot just works.

**This is the slow step**, especially on shared Wi-Fi. It's done when your prompt comes back. **Download the notebook
(step 6) while you wait.**

## 6. Download the notebook {#notebook}

- [Download the learner notebook]({{< var download.learner >}}){download="" data-noresolveinput=""}: blank code to write with us. This is the
  one you need.
- [Download the filled notebook]({{< var download.filled >}}){download="" data-noresolveinput=""}: every answer, to check your work.

Your browser saves them in your Downloads folder.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Prefer the terminal?

Run one of these inside `dss-python`, once step 5 has finished (or in a second terminal window). The notebook lands in
your project folder, so you can skip dragging it in (step 7).

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Mac

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
curl -LO https://ncsu-libraries.github.io/dsti-python/notebooks/introduction-to-programming-with-python.ipynb
```
:::

### Windows (PowerShell)

Type `curl.exe`, with the `.exe`. Plain `curl` in PowerShell is a different tool.

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```powershell
curl.exe -LO https://ncsu-libraries.github.io/dsti-python/notebooks/introduction-to-programming-with-python.ipynb
```
:::
:::
:::

## 7. Start JupyterLab and open the notebook

Once step 5 is finished, run this in `dss-python`:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv run jupyter lab
```
:::

Your browser opens JupyterLab. **Leave the terminal open.** It's running JupyterLab.

1. Open your Downloads folder, and drag the notebook onto JupyterLab's file list in the left sidebar. Or click the
   **Upload** button (↑) above the file list, and choose the file.
2. Double-click the notebook to open it.
3. Scroll to **1. Python and JupyterLab**. Click the bar plot cell under **Example: a simple bar plot**, and press
   {{< kbd Shift-Enter >}}.

**A chart means it all works:** Python, JupyterLab and matplotlib. No chart by about 9:30? Flag a helper, or switch to
Colab ([step 10](#colab)) and keep going.

## 8. Stop, and start again later

Save your work with {{< kbd Cmd-S >}} (Mac) or {{< kbd Ctrl-S >}} (Windows).

To stop JupyterLab, go back to the terminal and press {{< kbd Ctrl-C >}} twice.

Next time, open a terminal and run:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
cd dss-python
uv run jupyter lab
```
:::

Then double-click your notebook in the file list.

## 9. Alternative: conda {#conda}

Already use Anaconda, Miniconda or Miniforge? Use these commands instead of steps 2 to 5. We show uv in the room, but
helpers can still help you with conda.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Mac

Open Terminal: press {{< kbd Cmd-Space >}}, type **Terminal**, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}.

### Windows

Open **Anaconda Prompt** or **Miniforge Prompt** from the Start menu. Plain PowerShell usually doesn't know `conda`.
:::

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
{{< var conda.create >}}
conda activate dss-python
mkdir dss-python
cd dss-python
jupyter lab
```
:::

- The first command is one long line. Use the copy button.
- `-c conda-forge --override-channels` uses only the conda-forge channel. It skips Anaconda's default channel, so
  conda won't ask you to accept its Terms of Service.
- `python={{< var python >}}` matches uv and Colab.
- The conda download is bigger and slower than uv's. Start it early.

The last command opens JupyterLab. Now download the notebook (step 6), drag it into the file list, double-click it, and
run the bar plot cell (step 7). Skip the `uv run jupyter lab` command: JupyterLab is already running.

**Next time**, in the same kind of terminal:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
conda activate dss-python
cd dss-python
jupyter lab
```
:::

**To add a package**, with `dss-python` active:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
conda install -c conda-forge polars
```
:::

No conda yet? We suggest uv, so use steps 2 to 5. If you want conda anyway,
[Miniforge](https://conda-forge.org/download/) has a Mac installer (`.pkg`) and a Windows installer (`.exe`).

## 10. Backup: Google Colab {#colab}

Colab runs in your browser, so there's nothing to install. Use it if your install is stuck, or on a Chromebook or
tablet.

1. Open the [learner notebook in Colab]({{< var colab.learner >}}).
2. Sign in with your Google account.
3. Click **Copy to Drive** in the toolbar.
4. Work in the new tab, titled **Copy of introduction-to-programming-with-python.ipynb**.

A "not authored by Google" warning means you're in the original tab. Switch to your copy.

### Move your Colab work to your laptop

Haven't installed Python yet? Do steps 1 to 5 first. Then, in Colab, choose **File → Download → Download .ipynb**. Start
JupyterLab as in step 7 and drag the file into its file list.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `uv: command not found` | Open a new terminal. Still missing on a Mac? Run `source $HOME/.local/bin/env`. |
| "running scripts is disabled" (Windows) | Use the exact command shown above, with `-ExecutionPolicy ByPass`. |
| Antivirus or SmartScreen blocks the install | Flag a helper, or ask at [go.ncsu.edu/getdatahelp]({{< var help >}}). |
| Mac "command line developer tools" prompt | Click **Not Now**. You don't need them. |
| The download is slow | Keep going in Colab ([step 10](#colab)). You can finish the install during the break. |
| The browser didn't open | Copy the `http://localhost:…` link from the terminal and paste it into your browser. |
| The notebook isn't in JupyterLab's file list | Drag it in again, and check you started JupyterLab inside `dss-python`. |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'matplotlib'` | This JupyterLab isn't your project's. Press {{< kbd Ctrl-C >}} twice, then run `cd dss-python`, then `uv run jupyter lab` (with `uv run`). |
| ``Failed to spawn: `jupyter` `` | Run `uv add jupyterlab matplotlib` in `dss-python` first. |
| A file named `…(1).ipynb` | It's a second download. Use either one. |
| Chromebook or tablet | Use the Colab backup ([step 10](#colab)). |
| `conda: command not found` (or "not recognized") | On Windows, use Anaconda Prompt or Miniforge Prompt. On a Mac, open a new terminal. |
| conda asks you to accept Terms of Service | Use the exact command shown in step 9, with `-c conda-forge --override-channels`. |
